_note: Module 19 of docs/PROMPT-CONTROL-TOWER-UI.md (§7.8, §8): every external API the platform talks to or has been asked to talk to, as a card the API Registry screen would draw, with the shape of a key's metadata, the actions a card offers, and the flows of data that reach each provider. Proposed 24 September 2026, Phase 2 of that plan: a contract and its build checks. Restated against the tree on 1 October 2026, because two earlier readings of this note were each wrong about it. The API Registry screen reads this contract: apps/web/src/features/portal/gilbertone/ApiRegistry.tsx draws its cards, card statuses and refusals from it. Five of the six actions have handlers, for the founder alone, since 28 September 2026: enable and disable are POST /v1/founder/providers/{card}/enabled, rotate-key is PUT and DELETE /v1/founder/providers/{card}/key, test is POST /v1/founder/providers/{card}/test and view-logs is GET /v1/founder/providers/{card}/logs, beside GET /v1/founder/providers — declared in packages/catalog/apis/assistant.json, handled in apps/assistant-api/src/server.ts over the key vault in apps/assistant-api/src/lib/provider-vault.ts, behind a founder session, with a fresh authenticator code on every write and no key in any answer. They reach the six cards that vault names (packages/catalog/founder-access.json#vault), and packages/catalog/control-tower-portal.json draws them as founder controls. Outside a founder session, and on a card the vault holds no slot for, the five are drawn shut; configure-scopes has no handler and is drawn disabled with its gate's refusal (apps/web/src/features/portal/gilbertone/Controls.tsx). The plan's three files — secret-vault.ts, key-registry.ts and provider-health.ts — do not exist: provider-vault.ts is the vault, and a test is one call made on the founder's press, not a health-check runner. What the platform calls: Azure OpenAI and Azure Speech in southafricanorth from the assistant service in production; ElevenLabs, Alibaba Qwen's speech and recognition and OpenAI's hosted Whisper are built in the same service and configured nowhere, so nothing calls them until a key is set and the residency rule admits them; from a browser, OpenFreeMap's tiles when somebody switches the street map on, which need no key, and Mapbox's when a build was given VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN (packages/catalog/map-providers.json), which this file cannot see and records as not-configured. Ollama, Qdrant and the three knowledge sources have adapters and are dark. Every payment, SMS, push, email and device-gateway provider the plan lists, and the maps providers other than those two, is proposed: nothing in any service can call one, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails the build the day code names one while its card still says so. The plan's wireframe shows keys, balances and credit for providers that are not configured; none of that is written here. When a provider is switched off, every route that depends on it answers with the capability's own not-connected sentence out of packages/catalog/capabilities.json — the discipline packages/catalog/feeds.json already keeps for its seams — and this file never writes a not-connected sentence of its own.
_gateWhy: docs/PROMPT-CONTROL-TOWER-UI.md §9: the secret vault built, the health-check runner tested, enable and disable tested, balance tracking tested. None is built. Nothing on a card below may be drawn as live until its part of G32 is.

cardStatuses.sentence: Nothing in MyThuso can call this provider. It is a name on a list.

speechSelection.why: Added 28 September 2026 with the second and third speech providers. Each variable names a card below by id, per direction; unset means the default, which is the one provider with a South African region. A value that is not a built speech card serving that direction refuses the service at start-up, naming the cards it could have been (apps/assistant-api/src/lib/speech.ts). These are the service's own switches rather than a card's credential, so they are named here and not in any card's environment, and deploy/ops/configure-assistant-env.sh does not write them: selecting where a patient's voice goes is a decision written by hand, like the production acknowledgement.

pricing.why: Azure's list price for neural text to speech on the standard tier, per million characters, copied from the pricing page by hand on the day recorded. The day the figure is checked again, this record is the one to change.

cards.name: ElevenLabs
cards._environmentWhy: The key and the region as every provider's; then the provider's own identifier for the voice that reads under each of the contract's two labels, and for the administrator's own recorded voice (packages/catalog/voice.json#ownVoice). Voice identifiers are the account's own library, not a public list, and one of them identifies a person, so none is written in this repository: the adapter reads them from the environment, a label with no identifier answers voiceUnavailable, and the own voice is used only where the own-voice setting names the register.
cards._modelsWhy: Of the contract's five languages, which each model is documented to speak, read from the vendor's text-to-speech model page and its v3 language list on 2026-09-28, not measured: Multilingual v2 lists 29 languages and Flash v2.5 the same 29 with three more, English among them and no South African language; Eleven v3 lists Afrikaans. None lists isiZulu, isiXhosa or Sesotho, so those are answered voiceUnavailable whichever model is chosen. Which model reads is the elevenlabs-model setting in packages/catalog/voice.json.

regions.why: ElevenLabs serves from the United States by default and offers isolated environments in the European Union, India and Singapore to enterprise customers only, each with its own account and key; the vendor's own documentation says processing may still occur outside the selected location. Nowhere in South Africa. GilbertOne's spoken answer sent to any of the four is a cross-border transfer of special personal information under POPIA section 72, and the section 72 register has no basis for it.

cards.voicesFrom: The account's own voice library, named by identifier in the service's environment per label (ELEVENLABS_VOICE_FEMALE, ELEVENLABS_VOICE_MALE) and for the administrator's own voice (ELEVENLABS_VOICE_OWN); the door still admits only the contract's own voice names, which the adapter resolves to a label and then to the identifier.

ownVoice.why: The one provider on file that carries a person's own recorded voice. Recording it happens in the vendor's console, by the administrator, with the consent voice.json records; nothing here uploads audio.

shapesFrom.why: The request — POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id} with the key in the xi-api-key header, output_format and optimize_streaming_latency in the query, text, model_id, language_code and voice_settings in the body — and the audio reading were written from the published reference on 2026-09-28 and not tried against the live API in the change that built them; the adapter's header says so.

pricing.why: ElevenLabs sells monthly plans with characters included and charges the figures above for characters beyond them, read from the pricing page by hand on the day recorded. The per-million figure is the pay-as-you-go rate for Multilingual v2 and v3 — ten cents a thousand characters — recorded rather than a plan's cheaper included rate, so the preview never understates what a reading might cost; Flash is half of it. A list price and not a measurement: no bill has been read.

cards.audioRetainedByProvider: The vendor logs requests by default (enable_logging) and documents a zero-retention mode for enterprise plans; the adapter sends enable_logging=false on every request and the residency decision must weigh what the vendor keeps regardless.
cards._gateWhy: G33 is the residency gate: a signed residency decision (docs/governance/DATA-RESIDENCY-OPTIONS.md §7), the section 72 register updated and a DPA executed. Until it closes the adapter may be configured in development only; apps/assistant-api/src/lib/speech.ts refuses to select it in production.

cards.why: Built 28 September 2026 on the founder's ask and configured nowhere. showMetadataToggle.sentence: Show metadata switches between the masked last four and the last four with its fingerprint. It never shows the key. The full key exists only in the vault.
showMetadataToggle.why: The plan's mask and unmask toggle is a display convenience, not a security boundary. A toggle that could reveal the key would put it in the browser, which the vault exists to prevent.

entry.sentence: The key is typed into a password field, submitted once over TLS to the vault, and never shown again.
entry.why: Every place a key is shown is a place it can be copied from.

actions.why: Switching an API off is a first-class control. The safe state already exists — it is what the service does with nothing configured — so disabling is a return to it, not a new failure mode.
A new key is entered once; the old one is revoked at the provider and its metadata kept for the audit.
A minimal call that reports pass or fail and latency. For a paid provider it shows its estimated cost first, like the voice preview.

residencySelector.sentence: Choosing a South African region records that processing is onshore. It does not determine section 72 for support access, backups or telemetry, which DATA-RESIDENCY-OPTIONS.md §4 lists as open questions even for an onshore region. Choosing Tier 2 or Tier 3 requires a DPA reference before the provider can be saved.
residencySelector.why: The plan says the Tier 1 choice auto-populates the section 72 determination. A dropdown cannot make a legal determination; it can record which question has been answered and which has not.

_dataFlowsWhy: Every route in packages/catalog/apis/assistant.json that sends a request field to an external provider, tagged by whether it may carry health information. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds each flow to a built route and a real field, refuses a health-information flow to a Tier 3 provider or to any provider that is not built, and reports — without failing, because it is production's state and not a code defect — how many health-information flows reach a provider with no residency decision. Today that is all of them, which is the gap docs/governance/ASSISTANT-ACTIVATION.md records.

refusals.statement: A provider that is not configured, or has been disabled, is never called. Every route that depends on it answers the capability's own not-connected sentence, or the deterministic layer's answer.
refusals.why: A switch that turns a provider off on the screen and leaves it callable in code is a switch that lies. Until the enable and disable controls exist, the build holds the stronger rule: a provider this file records as proposed has no code that could call it at all.

refusals.statement: A request field that may carry health information is never sent to a provider whose residency tier is contractual.
refusals.why: Health information is special personal information under POPIA. A contractual transfer is the weakest of the three tiers, and the one a hospital's Information Officer is least able to verify.

refusals.statement: A provider's key never reaches the browser, in full or in part beyond its last four characters and a fingerprint prefix. No health or status route carries anything but booleans, a mode and counts.
refusals.why: The vault is the security boundary and the mask is a convenience. A key in a browser is a key in every extension, every screenshot and every support session.

refusals.statement: No balance, credit or usage figure is shown for a provider until it has been read from that provider or counted by the service.
refusals.why: The plan's wireframe shows balances for providers nothing can call. A figure on a card is read as a fact about money.

refusals.statement: Choosing a region records where processing happens. It never records a section 72 determination; that is recorded by the responsible party, with its basis, in DATA-RESIDENCY-OPTIONS.md §7.
refusals.why: Support access, backups, logs and telemetry can cross a border from an onshore region. A form that treated a region as the answer would close a question nobody had asked.

refusals.statement: A patient's capture and GilbertOne's spoken answer are health information. In production they are not sent to a speech provider with no South African region while docs/governance/DATA-RESIDENCY-OPTIONS.md §7 has no option chosen. The Information Officer and the responsible party sign that decision; no environment variable stands in for it.
refusals.why: Two speech providers with no South African region were built on 28 September 2026 so they can be tested; the residency decision is the only thing that may let a patient's voice cross a border. apps/assistant-api/src/lib/speech.ts reads this statement, refuses the selection at start-up in its words and falls back to the default provider or to the speech-not-configured refusal, rather than using the provider quietly. An acknowledgement variable was considered and refused: who decides is written in that document's first section, and it is not an operator with root.

refusals.statement: A card never writes its own not-connected sentence. It names a capability, and the sentence is rendered from packages/catalog/capabilities.json word for word.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/feeds.json's the-notice-comes-from-the-capability rule, for the same reason: when an integration lands, one boolean changes and the sentence stops being said everywhere on the same day.

preview: No key has been entered, rotated or revoked through any screen, no provider has been enabled or disabled from one, and no balance has been read. Azure OpenAI and Azure Speech are configured in production, OpenFreeMap's tiles are asked for from the browser without a key, Ollama, Qdrant and the knowledge sources are built and dark, OpenAI Whisper, Alibaba Qwen-ASR, Alibaba Qwen-TTS and ElevenLabs are built and configured nowhere — and refused in production for patient audio until the residency decision is signed — and every other card is a name in a plan.
